title: MCP servers can now ship skills, run long tasks, request sign-off, and receive files
summary: Connect Claude to an MCP server and the server no longer just lists its tools. It can send over its playbook too: skills load only when needed, long tasks run in the background, critical actions pause for your approval, and files go straight through without touching the context window.
ai_summary: Anthropic has added four capabilities to MCP. The centerpiece is Skills over MCP: servers publish skills alongside their tools, Claude loads them only when needed, and they update with the server; it is now in public beta. Tasks and Elicitation are generally available: Tasks lets servers run long jobs in the background, while Elicitation pauses actions such as spending money or deleting data for user confirmation. File Uploads is rolling out soon: PDFs, spreadsheets, and images go directly to a server, bypassing the context window. On the ecosystem side, monthly MCP SDK downloads top 700 million and there are more than 10,000 connectors; on-demand tool search can cut context use by over 85% in multi-server setups. Pro, Max, and Ultra plans get Skills by default, Team admins can enable it, and Enterprise support is coming soon.
brief: Skills over MCP is now in public beta: skills ship and update with the server, and Claude loads them only when needed.
Tasks and Elicitation are generally available: long tasks run in the background, and actions like spending money or deleting data pause for confirmation.
File Uploads is rolling out soon: PDFs, spreadsheets, and images go straight to the server without passing through the context window.
Scale: MCP sees more than 700 million SDK downloads per month; on-demand tool search in multi-server setups can cut context use by over 85%.

cover.headline: MCP servers can now ship skills
cover.highlight: Plus run long tasks, ask for confirmation, and accept files

sections.h: What it is: MCP servers go from tool catalogs to partners

blocks.p: MCP stands for Model Context Protocol, a standard interface that lets Claude connect to your company's data and applications. Anthropic released it two years ago, and it has become a common connectivity layer in the agent ecosystem. In one sentence: MCP servers no longer just list tool names; they can now behave more like another agent, sharing skills with Claude, taking on long tasks, pausing for confirmation, and receiving files directly.

Rollout status comes in three tiers: Skills over MCP is in public beta; Tasks and Elicitation are generally available (GA); File Uploads is coming soon. All four capabilities are part of the open MCP spec and its extensions, so once a server supports them, any compatible client can use them, not just Claude.

sections.h: Four new capabilities, and the gaps they fill

blocks.p: Taken together, they close the same gap: before, Claude and a server mostly exchanged tool calls and results, which ruled out many real business actions. Now a server can share its playbook, take on long-running work, ask a human mid-task, and accept files directly, making it more like a long-term partner.

fig.text: Claude can work with a server more like it works with another agent: learning from it, delegating to it, and exchanging input and files along the way.

sections.h: Skills: shipping the how-to, not just the tool

blocks.p: Tool names and descriptions tell Claude what a server has, not how to handle a job well. A CRM server may expose a 'look up customer' tool, but a full onboarding flow for new customers is hard to explain through tool descriptions alone.

Skills over MCP lets servers package that know-how into skills and publish them alongside tools. A skill can contain best practices, step-by-step workflows, or even playbooks tailored to a specific account or organization. Two user-friendly details: Claude loads a skill only when it's needed, so the context window doesn't fill up; and skills update with the server, so developers ship tools and guidance together and users have nothing extra to install.

list: Already using it:
Shopify: lets Claude design and update a merchant's online store end to end.
HubSpot: onboards new customers and gets them set up inside Claude.
Atlassian: lets Claude draw on deep organizational context for insights and work analysis.
Carta: will draft and issue equity from an uploaded document (coming soon).

sections.h: Tasks and Elicitation: long jobs in the background, confirmation for critical actions

blocks.p: Tasks is for long-running work. Before, a tool call had to finish before Claude could move on. Now servers can run time-consuming operations in the background, even full agent loops, while Claude keeps working and picks up the result when it's ready. ZoomInfo uses it for deeper account and contact research that previously required several prompts.

Elicitation is for the mid-call human sign-off. Some actions need user consent, such as spending money or deleting data. A server can pause mid-call, ask for input through a form or link, then continue where it left off.

sections.h: File Uploads: large files without the context hit

blocks.p: File Uploads lets Claude pass files to MCP servers, not just text. The key point: PDFs, spreadsheets, and images go directly to the server, bypassing the context window. That means large files no longer eat into the model's limited attention, and it makes handing files to the server for processing much smoother.
Like Skills, it's part of the open extensions. It is rolling out soon, starting with Pro, Max, and Ultra plans and eligible Team and Enterprise plans.

sections.h: What else changed under the hood this year

blocks.p: Beyond the four new capabilities, Anthropic also outlined improvements to MCP's foundations, all aimed at making production use cheaper and easier to manage.

list: More token-efficient: tool search loads tool definitions only when needed, which can cut the context they use by more than 85% in multi-server setups.
Easier to scale: the latest MCP spec is stateless and supported across Claude products, so servers are easier to maintain as they grow.
Simpler to authorize: the Enterprise Managed Auth extension lets admins authorize supported servers once, so users connect automatically.
More interactive: the MCP Apps extension brings full interfaces into Claude, beside the conversation or in full screen.

blocks.p: Pricing: the announcement doesn't list separate pricing for these capabilities or plan prices; it only says which plans include them. Enterprise pricing requires contacting Anthropic sales.

list: Pricing: no separate pricing for the four capabilities, and no plan prices.
File Uploads has no specific launch date, just 'rolling out soon.'
No specific date for Skills on Enterprise, just 'coming soon.'
The 'over 85%' figure is for multi-server setups; the announcement doesn't say how much a single server saves.
The announcement doesn't detail how skills differ from tools on permissions or token billing.
Carta's equity feature is only marked 'coming soon,' with no date.

blocks.p: Value: for teams that connect Claude to business systems, this update lowers the cost of teaching Claude how your company works and handing it long-running jobs. The tradeoff: Team and Enterprise plans either need an admin to enable features or have to wait longer.

callout.title: By role
list: Pro / Max / Ultra users: you can try Skills, Tasks, and Elicitation now; just connect to servers that support them.
Team admins: enable Skills from the admin console; Tasks and Elicitation are rolling out gradually.
Server developers: follow the official docs to add Skills, Tasks, Elicitation, and File Uploads support. Because these are open specs, other compatible clients can use them once you do.
If context and cost are your focus: look first at File Uploads and on-demand tool search; both are about saving context.
